Lineage · milestone report

R4 — Atmosphere

The light of the owner's presence, what glows in the dark, the island's own weather and the weather of its events, what those events leave on the land, and the end of a world. Every effect is filmed from the real renderer in all three views (map, middle view, up close) at the desk screen's own size, 1024×600, and at 30 frames a second, the board's target. The scene is stepped one frame at a time on its own clock, so no frame is dropped however busy the PC is. The apocalypse is the exception to the three views: it is shown on the map only, since it holds the camera there. The events are the sim's own, recorded with tools/stream.py --stage from the v9 fixture two weeks on, so what each leaves is what the sim does.

Where the films are. They are VP9 WebM videos (4:4:4 colour, so pixel edges stay hard) in films/ beside this page. That folder is not committed: it is about 150 MB, and npm run atmosphere writes it again. Without it, each film shows its poster, a still from its middle.

The sim: the island's own weather, and fire that burns animals

The owner chose these in round 2 and they were built in R4 (schema v12, ADR 0021). M11's algae took v11; this branch carries it.

  • Weather (weather.py, a new subsystem ticked hourly before the fire). Rain spells begin at random, at 5, 3, 6 and 5 a month in spring, summer, autumn and winter, and last 2 to 30 hours. Of the spells, 30 % carry thunder (seen only) and 12 % are thunderstorms, lasting 1 to 6 hours.
  • Lightning only in a thunderstorm. [flora] fire_strikes_per_storm_hour = 1.6 strikes per storm-hour at full dryness. That gives the same expected strikes a year (about 10.7 on the default calendar) as the old 30 ignitions a year. Fires start only while it rains, and any rain slows a fire as wet land does. The rain power is a soaking rain that puts fires out and never strikes.
  • Fire burns animals: [fauna] fire_damage_per_hour = 1.0 of an animal's capacity, so an hour in a burning land cell kills it. Swimmers are safe, and the burnt leave no carrion.

The office fortnight below (office.json) holds 1 cloud, 2 soaking spells.

the light (0–1)owner at the deskrainthunderthunderstormthe rain power

The light

A tint multiplied over the land, plants and animals. Night is moonlit blue, dusk (the owner away) is rose, dawn (the owner back) is lilac, and the day is graded by the season. Each of the sim's 10-minute steps is eased in over the time before the next.

Glow

Light added over the tint, breathing slowly (3.5 s), faint enough closer in that the animal is clearly seen through it (from 12 % to 30 % in the middle view, 6 % to 16 % up close). Here, two animals with the glow gene at night, sent to the scene as the stream would send them (the fixture's world has none). On the map, a small light just round each animal's square. In the middle and local views, a ring of light round the body whose heart is clear, so that the animal itself is seen; up close the ring is wider.

Rain, thunder and thunderstorms

Each is a staged spell of the sim's own weather. Cloud blocks the sun while it rains: the world's colours are graded toward grey and cooled (a colour-matrix filter), the light dims, and a faint grey haze lies over it; a storm greys and darkens most. The drops are pale blue streaks drawn over the light, so that they show on any ground, sized to the view (3 pixels on the map, 5 in the middle view, 6 up close), in three layers at different sizes and speeds, leaning with the wind. Each spell falls with its own strength, swelling and easing within it. Rings spread where drops hit the water, and drops splash on the land, in the middle view and up close. With thunder, a thin bolt at random times and a faint flash: it starts nothing. A thunderstorm is bigger: a darker sky, half as much rain again, faster and leaning harder, gusts that swing the wind and every layer of rain with it, forked bolts in bursts and lulls, and brighter flashes. The rain power's soaking rain is steadier and leans least.

Rain

Rain with thunder

A thunderstorm

The rain power

An overcast sky

Between rains the sky clouds over now and then (8 spells a month, 3 to 36 hours): the day greys a little less than under rain, and nothing falls. It is only seen: plants and animals live under the same light, and fire is not slowed.

Fire

A thunderstorm at 02:00 on the office schedule (night), its lightning striking cell (127, 103): the biggest bolt, thick and forked, with the brightest flash. Flames then rise from every burning cell under a wide glow, with embers and smoke. Up close each cell has two large six-frame flames, flickering slowly (about 4 frames a second) and see-through (72 %), so what stands behind them shows, with three small flames licking round them; the large ones are drawn after pixel-art fire references: a steady base on its fuel, a body that sways more the higher it is, tongues licking up in turn and a lick pinching off at the top, a deep red rim around a white-gold heart. Each has its own glow and sparks, and stands in a bed of glowing embers. The flames are sorted among the plants: a tree in front covers the fire behind it, and a burning tree or bush burns in its crown too. An animal that dies in the fire leaves a puff of ash. Then the fire spreads, at a sim-day in 12 s. Two sim-days later the burnt land is charcoal ground, drawn cell by cell where the fire went, with drifts of ash, a ragged edge and the skeletons of the trees that stood.

The strike

The fire spreading (time-lapse)

A larger fire, made up

The sim's fires are often small, as this one is (it burnt 4 cells in 18 hours); how far they spread is M11's to tune. To show the fire's look at a larger scale, here are 24 cells set alight on demand (?show=night,fire), with the thunderstorm and the strike that come with it. They are chosen as the sim's fire spreads: from cell to neighbouring cell, only where plants carry it, the most flammable fuel first. Only the land is the sim's.

What it leaves

Volcano

Staged at cell (128, 75) with the terrain's own apply_volcano. The sim raises a cone in the heights and bares the land round it (1.4 times its radius, for 120 days, so no plant stands on it). The ground's gentle shading hardly shows a cone from above, so the scene draws it, after how top-down pixel-art games draw mountains (Zelda: A Link to the Past, the Pokémon GBA overworlds, Stardew Valley): stacked basalt ledges with lit, grainy tops and cliff faces toward the viewer, boulders, and a mouth whose back wall shows. Round its foot a skirt of ash and scree thins into the ground. While it erupts, its lava is a layer of its own, a crusted pool and rivers meandering down the ledges, and it flows: eight looped frames of crust welling up in the middle of the pool and drifting outward to its rim, and down the rivers, the heat swelling and ebbing. The scree lies under the plants and the cone stands among them, so trees in front of it are drawn over it. Above it rise an ash column and embers. The cone stays drawn for 30 sim-days.

Earthquake

Staged at cell (128, 75) (apply_earthquake): the picture jolts for 4 s, dying away, and dust rises over the fault.

Meteor

The meteor god power, pressed at 02:00; the sim aimed it at cell (162, 118). A streak from high up, a flash as it strikes, a glow and dust; every animal within twice its radius is killed. The bowl it digs shows only once the meteor has struck (the land the stream sends with it waits until then), and the sim bares the land round it. Its thrown earth lies under the plants. It is drawn from a height field lit from the upper left, after how simple craters look from above (a bowl with a raised rim of thrown-out earth and uplifted rock, a rumpled ejecta blanket that thins outward, rays thrown away from the impact's direction, walls that slump): a rim scalloped where it slumped, the near wall in its shadow, the far wall lit, a slumped lobe on the floor, pale ejecta with boulders thinning into clods, and rays downrange of the meteor, none uprange.

Seed

The seed god power sows 400 seeds of random genomes on bare land across the whole island; the sim does not aim it. On the screen, golden motes drift down onto the bare cells in sight. In the land the sim sends with the power, every cell it sowed sprouts: each sprout breaks the soil with a glint of gold and grows leaf by leaf over three seconds, and stays until the cell's plants are big enough to be drawn. The films are at cell (240, 84), where most seeds took.

Sown on burnt ground, made up

The island in this save has little bare land, so the sim's seeds took on a few scattered cells. Here, made up on the land (?show=day,burnt,seed), the seed falls on ground a fire has just bared: every bare cell in reach sprouts, as the sim sows them, and the sprouts grow leaf by leaf.

Ark

The ark god power brings 12 plant eaters, landing on a vegetated spot. The light comes down where the stream says they landed (creatures_arrived, at cell (45, 27)), as wide as the place they land on in every view, fading at its foot into a pool of light on the ground. Each newcomer comes into being there: a thread of light comes down onto it, flares, and leaves sparks rising while it fades in, in steps, over 2.5 s.

Algae, waves and the tide

M11's algae on the shallow sea, two weeks after the save: olive fronds in clumps, as thick as their biomass. Waves come in as one front from one side of the sea and sweep across the island at 5 cells a second, so neighbouring stretches of coast break a moment apart and far ones at their own time. Each wave, every 5 s: a line far out, one nearer, the foam breaking at the shore, then the swash running up the beach in three steps and draining back, smoothly, as far as the tide (turning over a minute) lets it. The map has the surf without a swash. The films are on the coast by the thickest algae, 30 s.

The end of a world

From end.json, where the herd starves on day 2 and the sim ends the world. The film is the whole three-minute sequence at the screen's own frame rate. It plays on the map only, since it holds the camera there.

Tests

Python: weather (spell rates by season, kinds and lengths, the fire told each hour, state), lightning only in storms, rain slowing a fire, fire killing animals, the v11 to v12 migration and fixture, the stream's staging and lands after events.

Left for later

  • R5 measures all of this on the board. During a fire, up to a few hundred flames and halos are drawn; rain draws 180 drops and up to 80 ripples. R5 also tunes the look, the cone among it.
  • Sanity checks: the ark lands only on land now (a fix in this round), and the seed sows only bare land; a milestone checking such rules across the sim was proposed to the owner.
  • A volcano's cone and a meteor's crater are drawn for 30 sim-days from their event. A renderer that connects later sees only the land's own shading, because the wire carries no "volcano" fact.
  • M11 re-checks fire frequency, mortality and chronicle numbers once R4 is in main.
